chapter: Cotton Club and radio fame with Cab
title: Harold Arlen's Black blues feeling
summary: Thomas says Arlen had the blues talent; they discuss 'Stormy Weather', 'Get Happy', Arlen as a rehearsal pianist and singer, and his Cotton Club shows.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: [PAUSE]
Thomas - 111
Harold Arlen had that Black Blues thing.
Yeah, right. Because it was amazing when he wrote 'Stormy Weather.' It's not really nothin' but a Blues. [SINGS REFRAIN]
Well, someplace along the line, I think either Harold told me or somebody told me that he used to be a rehearsal piano player for Fletcher Henderson.
Maybe he did.
Which one of the famous tunes did he write? He didn't write 'Strike Up The Band,' did he. But he wrote something fast like that.
'Get Happy' was a big song for him.
[SINGS REFRAIN] Was that his tune?
Mmm-hmm, that was his tune.
I think he told me that he got tired of playing that [SINGS REFRAIN IN STRAIGHT TIME], so he just did ...[SINGS 'GET HAPPY' IN SYNCOPATION]
[LAUGHS, SINGS ALONG]
..(?).. to sit there and rehearse. Now, that's one of the stories that goes around.

Because he used to go away in the summertime, and he'd come back in the Fall with a show. Because he wrote such... He gave us so many great songs. But he didn't write 'World On A String.' [INCORRECT. HE DID.] Oh, he came
Thomas - 112
up with some many good things for ...(? )...
He wrote the song for ...(? )... and "Don't Worry About Me." Was that his song?
No, he didn't write "Don't Worry About Me." There was another guy downtown who wrote "Don't Worry About Me." Oh, he wrote some great songs. Not "Am I Blue?"
I did an album with him where he sings.
Yeah, he was a good singer.
He was a marvelous singer.
He was a good singer.
A good singer. At least he could express himself.
Yeah, right. That's how he got the job with the Cotton Club. He came up and did an audition, and then he sounded so good doing his own thing...
